title: Core pipeline
blurb: Students, judges, scoring, personas, juries and debate.

blocks.lead: CLI entry-point: run a single student model across datasets.

about.html: example: python scripts/run_student.py --student qwen2.5-32b --datasets gsm8k math
The study uses two students, qwen2.5-32b and llama3.1-8b. Run the script once for each (all eight closed-ended datasets by default).

blocks.usage:
python scripts/run_student.py --student STUDENT \
    [--datasets DATASETS [DATASETS ...]] [--num-samples NUM_SAMPLES] \
    [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] [--tensor-parallel-size TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE] \
    [--gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION]

actions.help: Student model key from student_models in models.yaml
Closed-ended datasets to solve (default: all 8). Open-ended datasets (SummEval, MT-Bench) use run_scoring_judge.py.
actions.default: gsm8k gsm_plus math arc_easy arc_challenge hellaswag winogrande truthfulqa

blocks.lead: CLI entry-point: run a single judge model across student solutions.

about.html: example: python scripts/run_judge.py --judge qwen3-4b --max-tokens 10 8192

One process per judge: run it once for each key under judge_models in slmjury/configs/models.yaml (and large_judge_models for the large judges). Existing judgement files are skipped unless --force is given.

blocks.usage:
python scripts/run_judge.py --judge JUDGE \
    [--max-tokens MAX_TOKENS [MAX_TOKENS ...]] \
    [--solutions-dir SOLUTIONS_DIR] [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] \
    [--datasets DATASETS [DATASETS ...]] \
    [--students STUDENTS [STUDENTS ...]] [--force] \
    [--tensor-parallel-size TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE] \
    [--gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION] \
    [--max-num-seqs MAX_NUM_SEQS]

actions.help: Only judge these datasets (default: every dataset found in --solutions-dir)
Only judge these students (default: every student in --solutions-dir)
Re-judge even if judgement files already exist
Override max_num_seqs from models.yaml (lower = less KV cache pressure)

blocks.lead: CLI entry-point: evaluate judgement files and generate summary reports.

about.html: examples: python scripts/run_evaluation.py --summary python scripts/run_evaluation.py --judge qwen3-4b --max-tokens 10

blocks.usage:
python scripts/run_evaluation.py [--judge JUDGE] [--max-tokens {10,8192}] \
    [--summary] [--judgements-dir JUDGEMENTS_DIR] [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] \
    [--summaries-dir SUMMARIES_DIR]

actions.help: Judge model key to evaluate, or 'all' (default: all)
Filter by max_tokens setting (default: both 10 and 8192)
Directory for the per-judge summaries written by --summary (the analyses in experiments/ read them from here)

blocks.lead: CLI entry-point: run scoring evaluation for open-ended datasets.

about.html: Scores SummEval, MT-Bench or both with one judge model per process. The model loads once; for MT-Bench it then scores every reference file it finds.

examples: python scripts/run_scoring_judge.py --judge qwen3-4b --datasets summeval python scripts/run_scoring_judge.py --judge qwen3-4b --datasets mtbench \ --reference-scores results/core/mtbench_references/ python scripts/run_scoring_judge.py --judge qwen3-4b --datasets summeval mtbench
Run it once per judge. MT-Bench needs the reference scores from scripts/run_mtbench_reference.py first.

blocks.usage:
python scripts/run_scoring_judge.py --judge JUDGE --datasets \
    {summeval,mtbench} [{summeval,mtbench} ...] [--max-tokens MAX_TOKENS] \
    [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] [--eval-dir EVAL_DIR] [--force] \
    [--reference-scores REFERENCE_SCORES] \
    [--tensor-parallel-size TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE] \
    [--gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION] \
    [--max-num-seqs MAX_NUM_SEQS]

actions.help: Datasets to score: summeval, mtbench or both
Re-score even if result files already exist
MT-Bench reference scores, one file or a directory of <reference>/<student>.json files (default: core/mtbench_references in the results folder)

blocks.lead: CLI entry-point: generate student model responses for MT-Bench (2 turns).

about.html: MT-Bench is open-ended: the student writes free-form responses to 80 questions, each with 2 turns. Turn 2 is a follow-up that depends on the model's Turn 1 response. The reference models (scripts/run_mtbench_reference.py) and the SLM judges then score these responses.
examples: python scripts/run_mtbench_student.py --student llama3.1-8b python scripts/run_mtbench_student.py --student qwen2.5-32b --tp 2 --gpu-mem 0.85
The study uses two students, qwen2.5-32b and llama3.1-8b. Run the script once for each.

blocks.usage:
python scripts/run_mtbench_student.py --student STUDENT \
    [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] [--force] \
    [--tensor-parallel-size TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE] \
    [--gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION]

actions.help: Student model key from student_models in models.yaml
Re-generate even if response file already exists

blocks.lead: CLI entry-point: score MT-Bench student responses with a reference model (Together API).

about.html: A large reference model, hosted on Together AI, scores each full 2-turn conversation once. It gets the same PROMPT_MTBENCH as the SLM judges, so a judge's correlation with the reference compares scores of the same prompt. Requests are retried with exponential backoff and spaced by a configurable delay. The reference models are listed under reference_models in slmjury/configs/models.yaml.

examples: python scripts/run_mtbench_reference.py --reference gpt-oss-120b \ --solutions-dir results/core/mtbench_responses/llama3.1-8b.json python scripts/run_mtbench_reference.py --reference qwen3.5-397b
Writes results/core/mtbench_references/<reference>/<student>.json. Each record uses the field names the scoring code reads.

blocks.usage:
python scripts/run_mtbench_reference.py [--solutions-dir SOLUTIONS_DIR] \
    --reference REFERENCE [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] \
    [--request-delay REQUEST_DELAY]

actions.help: Directory of student MT-Bench responses, or one response file (default: core/mtbench_responses in the results folder)
Reference model key from reference_models in models.yaml. Available: gpt-oss-120b, qwen3.5-397b
Directory for saving the reference scores
Override request_delay from models.yaml (seconds between calls)

blocks.lead: CLI entry-point: run one judge model with every persona system prompt.

about.html: Runs the judge with all 6 persona system prompts, over every student and dataset, at both token settings.
examples: python scripts/run_persona.py --judge qwen3-4b python scripts/run_persona.py --judge qwen3-4b --personas Strict Lenient --max-tokens 10
The study runs it once per judge for qwen3-4b, phi4mi-3.8b, llama3.1-8b, qwen3-14b and phi4-14b.

Writes results/core/personas/<judge>/<persona>_<student>_<dataset>_t<budget>.json. To score the verdicts against the ground truth (writes results/core/personas/evaluations/ and results/core/summaries/personas/), run: python scripts/run_strategy_evaluation.py --personas

blocks.usage:
python scripts/run_persona.py --judge JUDGE \
    [--personas PERSONAS [PERSONAS ...]] \
    [--max-tokens MAX_TOKENS [MAX_TOKENS ...]] \
    [--solutions-dir SOLUTIONS_DIR] [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] [--force] \
    [--tensor-parallel-size TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE] \
    [--gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION] \
    [--max-num-seqs MAX_NUM_SEQS]

actions.help: Re-run even if persona result files already exist
Override max_num_seqs from models.yaml (lower = less KV cache pressure)

blocks.lead: CLI entry-point: run debate configurations over every student and dataset.

about.html: A configuration is three agents: three different judges, or one judge at three temperatures (MAD_COMBINATIONS in slmjury/strategies/debate.py, numbered 0 to 9). The agents debate each item for up to 5 rounds until they agree. Items still split after the last round take the majority verdict.
examples: python scripts/run_debate.py --configs 0 python scripts/run_debate.py --configs 0,3,5 --tp 1 --gpu-mem 0.85 python scripts/run_debate.py --configs all

Writes results/core/debate/<configuration>/<student>_<dataset>.json. To score the verdicts against the ground truth (writes results/core/debate/evaluations/ and results/core/summaries/debate/), run: python scripts/run_strategy_evaluation.py --debate

blocks.usage:
python scripts/run_debate.py --configs CONFIGS \
    [--solutions-dir SOLUTIONS_DIR] [--output-dir OUTPUT_DIR] \
    [--max-tokens MAX_TOKENS] [--students STUDENTS [STUDENTS ...]] \
    [--datasets DATASETS [DATASETS ...]] [--force] \
    [--tensor-parallel-size TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE] \
    [--gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION] \
    [--max-num-seqs MAX_NUM_SEQS]

actions.help: Debate configuration index (0-9), a comma-separated list, or 'all'
Generation budget per agent turn (default: 8192; configurations 1, 2 and 4 mostly used 4096; see docs/REPRODUCE.md)
Only debate these students (default: every student in --solutions-dir)
Only debate these datasets (default: every dataset found in --solutions-dir)
Re-run even if debate result files already exist
Override max_num_seqs for all models (lower = less KV cache pressure)

blocks.lead: CLI entry-point: evaluate persona, jury (majority vote) and debate runs, and student accuracy.

about.html: scripts/run_evaluation.py covers the individual judges. This script does the same for the strategy runs. Every judgement file written by run_persona.py, by generate_all_ensembles() (juries) and by run_debate.py goes through JudgeEvaluator, which compares each verdict with the expected verdict from the ground truth. The per-file results are then summed into one summary per judge and budget (personas) or per panel or configuration (juries, debate). Accuracy is how often the verdict matches the ground truth, not how often the judge said Correct.

Reads, under <results>/core/ (<results> is --results-dir, which defaults to $SLMJURY_RESULTS if set, else results/): personas/<judge>/<persona>_<student>_<dataset>_t<budget>.json juries/<panel>/<student>_<dataset>.json debate/<configuration>/<student>_<dataset>.json student_solutions/<student>/<dataset>.json

Writes, under <results>/core/: personas/evaluations/<judge>/<persona>_<student>_<dataset>_t<budget>.json juries/evaluations/<panel>/<student>_<dataset>.json debate/evaluations/<configuration>/<student>_<dataset>.json summaries/personas/<judge>_t<budget>.json summaries/juries/<panel>.json summaries/debate/<configuration>.json summaries/student_accuracy.json
experiments/main_results/analyze.py reads the evaluation files.

about.code:
examples:
  python scripts/run_strategy_evaluation.py                 # all four steps
  python scripts/run_strategy_evaluation.py --personas --debate
  python scripts/run_strategy_evaluation.py --results-dir path/to/results

actions.help: Results folder; runs are read from and written to its core/ subfolder (default: $SLMJURY_RESULTS if set, else results)
